Somewhere in Africa, a power deal is signed in front of the cameras.

Today we sign for one hundred megawatts of power for our people!

We are ready to build, Minister.

Everyone applauds. But who in this room will carry the risk?

The MoU says the tariff is only indicative.

Every negotiation after today will start from that number.

Why does the trap persist, when everyone can describe it? Look at who is in the room at signature.

A visible answer to power shortages. And it costs us almost nothing today.

For me, it is an option on a site. And options can be sold.

The utility, which must pay, is often not a party. The ministry of finance is not in the room. The lenders arrive years later.
Exit one: the project stalls. Years of ministry time and developer spending produce no power. Sites stay locked up. A published tariff becomes a benchmark that later bidders must argue against.

Before we sign anything: who has reviewed it?

Finance has. Any support is sized to our fiscal space.

The utility has. We can pay for what we buy.

It is in the least-cost plan, with milestones and a sunset date.

Then we can lend against it.

Then we sign, and we publish it.

02
WHAT AN MoU BINDS,
AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
FACT
On its central commitment,
most MoUs bind no one.
RED TEAM
But in practice, an MoU creates four things
EXCLUSIVITYOver a site or a resource, sometimes for years.Competitors are kept out.
A TARIFF ANCHORAn indicative tariff or capacity, labelled non-binding.It becomes the reference point for every later negotiation.
PROMISES OF STATE HELPLand, permits, grid connection, support instruments.Expected before anyone has priced them.
A POLITICAL COMMITMENTA public signing, sometimes with a head of state.Harder to withdraw than any clause.
FACT
Three stages, three kinds of commitment
STAGE
WHAT BINDS
WHAT THE STATE HAS COMMITTED
MoU
Little in law; often exclusivity and confidentiality
A political signal; sometimes a site or a resource
Contract
Tariff, term and obligations of both parties, subject to conditions
Future payments, conditional on the plant reaching operation
Financial close
All of the above, now funded
Fixed obligations for the life of the contract
Source: author, Table 1.1
RED TEAM
The trap lies between
the MoU and financial close.
Some commitments never close. Others close on terms set when the project was least tested.
DECISION
Two tests are skipped at signature
THE LENDER'S TESTCan the project repay its debt?
THE STATE'S TESTCan the power system and the public finances carry the obligations for twenty years or more?

Source: World Bank 2014; TheCable 2020; Global Energy Monitor 2026
FACT
No one counts the MoUs
that went nowhere.
The denominator problem.
DECISION
Four explanations, read as layers
SPONSORThe developer lacks capital, experience or partners.Screen sponsors; limit exclusivity; attach milestones and securities.
PROCESSHow the project was originated.Compete by default; test unsolicited proposals against the plan.
SYSTEMThe plan, the grid and the buyer.Fix the system before adding contracts.
FISCALThe state's capacity to support.Apply the sovereign test; size support to fiscal space.
Not rivals. Layers. Which one binds first?
FACT

THE WAY OUT
Some projects cannot be tendered
at the outset.
Large hydropower · cross-border interconnectors · first projects in a new technology · small markets
FACT
Nachtigal, Cameroon: a joint development agreement,
and a local-currency tranche of unprecedented tenor.
Source: Power Technology 2021; IFC 2019
RED TEAM
2025: its payment guarantee was reported
largely drawn.
Source: Ecofin Agency 2025 (press; no official statement found)
DECISION
Not a ban. A better MoU.
CHECKEDAgainst the least-cost plan before signature
TIMEDWith milestones and a sunset date
REVIEWEDBy the utility and the ministry of finance, if it could lead to fixed obligations
PUBLISHEDIn a public register
is no longer a trap. It is a development tool.
RED TEAM
The five costs of the trap
1Power not delivered
2Better projects blocked
3Public attention consumed
4Credibility lost when terms are reopened
5Liabilities created when trapped projects close
DECISION
Four measures to close the trap
FILTER AT ENTRYNo MoU outside the least-cost plan unless tested against it
PRICE THE OPTIONDevelopment securities, milestones, sunset clauses
RISK BEARERS EARLYUtility and ministry of finance review any MoU that could lead to fixed payments or state support
PUBLISH A REGISTERPower MoUs and their status; let lapsed options expire
DECISION
Pricing the option is not enough on its own.
Close the trap at every point where the project is tested.
DECISION
The Sustainable Financial Close Test
A deal closes only when both the lender's test and the state's test are passed, and the state's answer is made public.
RED TEAM
What turns an MoU into a trap?
1Signed before either test is applied
2It costs its signatories almost nothing
3The risk bearers are absent at signature
Bring the risk bearers, and their tests,
to the start of the process.
BEFORE ANY POWER MoU IS SIGNED
01Is it in the least-cost plan, or tested against it?
02Does it carry milestones, a sunset date and, where appropriate, a development security?
03Have the utility and the ministry of finance reviewed it?
04Which layer could block it: sponsor, process, system or fiscal?
05Will it be published in the MoU register?
If not, it is not ready to sign.
AN MoU COSTS ALMOST NOTHING TO SIGN.
It can cost a great deal later.
Bring the risk bearers to the start.
